summary: This work numerically investigates spectator-qubit crosstalk in scaled-up fluxonium-transmon-fluxonium (FTF) architectures, finding that trivial scaling limits fidelity below 90%. The authors demonstrate that reducing coupling strength to $g_{FT}/2\pi = 200$ MHz and dynamically tuning inactive transmons to an off position suppresses spectator errors below $10^{-4}$ in 1D and 2D systems with up to six spectator qubits.
motivation: Recent experiments with the FTF architecture have demonstrated fast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates with ZZ suppression, but the scalability of this approach to larger qubit arrays like surface codes has not been thoroughly analyzed.
method: Using density matrix renormalization group for excited states (DMRG-X) tensor network simulations on systems up to ~$11 \times 10^6$ Hilbert space dimension (equivalent to 23 qubits), the authors compute eigenspectra and drive matrix elements for 1D chains, 2D grids, and $\llbracket 4,2,2 \rrbracket$ error-correcting code layouts, then time-evolve the center FTF pair under realistic drive pulses incorporating DRAG and compensating drives.
result: With optimized parameters ($g_{FT}/2\pi = 200$ MHz coupling, off-transmon detuning $\sim 300$ MHz above fluxonium $|1\rangle\leftrightarrow|2\rangle$), gate fidelities exceed $1 - 10^{-4}$ for 50–100 ns gates across all spectator configurations in both 1D and 2D layouts; transmon-to-transmon coupling up to $g_{TT}/2\pi = 40$ MHz and microwave crosstalk up to $\gamma \sim 0.3$ remain tolerable at 70–100 ns gate times.
